title: PHP Version Upgrade Breakage
description: Fix sites that break after the host upgrades PHP — deprecated functions, incompatible plugins, and version mismatch errors.

steps.title: Identify Current and Required PHP Version
steps.instructions: Check Site Health → Info for PHP version. Note WordPress minimum and each active plugin's PHP requirement. Host may have jumped multiple versions at once.

steps.title: Read PHP Error Logs for Deprecated Calls
steps.instructions: Look for 'deprecated', 'undefined function', or 'syntax error' in debug.log and host PHP logs. The file path usually identifies the offending plugin or theme.

steps.title: Test Target PHP Version on Staging
steps.instructions: Switch PHP version on staging clone before production. Run through homepage, admin, forms, and checkout. Never test PHP upgrades on live during business hours.

steps.title: Update All Plugins and Themes
steps.instructions: Most breakage is outdated code on new PHP. Update everything compatible. Replace abandoned plugins that have not been updated in 12+ months.

steps.title: Rollback PHP Temporarily if Critical
steps.instructions: If production is down, switch back to previous PHP version in hosting panel while fixing. Document deadline before host forces upgrade.

steps.title: Fix Custom Snippets and Child Theme Code
steps.instructions: Review functions.php, mu-plugins, and Code Snippets for removed PHP functions (each(), create_function(), etc.). Update to modern equivalents.

steps.title: Verify Required PHP Extensions
steps.instructions: New PHP versions may drop extensions (e.g. mysql, mcrypt). Confirm mysqli, curl, gd/imagick, zip, and intl are installed on the new version.

steps.title: Verify Site on New PHP Version
steps.instructions: Confirm no errors in logs after 24 hours on new PHP. Update client documentation with supported PHP version and next review date.
